newsitem.title: GERMANY: Commerzbank says no need for U.S. listing.
newsitem.headline: Commerzbank says no need for U.S. listing.

text.p: Germany's Commerzbank AG, forecasting a rise in operating earnings this year, said Tuesday it saw no need to list its shares in New York as several large German corporates have done, mainly because it did not wish to apply U.S. accounting rules.
Chairman Martin Kohlhaussen said banks, as service providers, were in a different position from companies that produced goods and had more to gain from a higher profile in the United States.
"I see no argument for a listing in New York," he told a news conference.

"We do not wish to have to issue double accounts," he said, referring to the system under which Daimler-Benz AG, for example, had last year to produce both German-standard accounts and results according to generally accepted U.S. principles.

Separately, the bank predicted operating earning would rise this year and said net interest and commission income jumped by 20 percent in January and February compared with the year-earlier period. Operating profit before risk provisions rose by 21.6 percent to 626 million marks ($364.9 million).
"We are completely satisfied with our profit and loss accounts for January and February '97," said Chief Executive Martin Kohlhaussen at the company's annual meeting.
